title: Merge room bookings
statement:
A meeting room's bookings are `[start, end]` pairs in no particular order. Two bookings that overlap or touch (one ends exactly when the other starts) should be merged into one.

Return the merged bookings sorted by start time.

clarifyingQuestions.question: Do bookings that touch count as overlapping?
clarifyingQuestions.why: Decides between < and <= in the comparison.

clarifyingQuestions.question: Can start equal end?
clarifyingQuestions.answer: Yes, a zero-length booking is allowed.

clarifyingQuestions.question: What should the output order be?

edgeCases.why: A booking inside another: the end must take the max, not the later booking’s end.
A chain of touching bookings merges into one.

approaches.name: Compare every pair repeatedly
approaches.idea: Merge any overlapping pair and repeat until nothing changes.
approaches.tradeoffs: Simple to state, slow and fiddly.

approaches.name: Sort by start, then sweep
approaches.idea: After sorting, overlaps can only happen with the most recent merged booking, so one pass suffices.

optimal.name: Sort and sweep
optimal.explanation: Sort by start. For each booking, if it starts at or before the end of the last merged booking, extend that end to the max of both ends; otherwise append it as a new merged booking.

hintLadder: If the bookings were in order of start time, which booking could the next one overlap with?
What happens to the merged end when one booking contains another?
Sort first. Then how many passes do you need?
Sort by start and keep extending the last merged booking while the next one starts before it ends.

expectedMentions.what: Proposes sorting by start then one sweep, O(n log n)
Explains why after sorting only the last merged booking can overlap
Uses the max of the ends to handle contained bookings
Traces a contained or chained example

followUps: Insert one new booking into an already merged, sorted list.
Return the free gaps between bookings in a day.

walkthrough.say: If one booking ends at 4 and the next starts at 4, do they merge? And the input isn’t sorted, but the output should be sorted by start?
If I sort by start time, any booking can only overlap the last merged one, because everything before it ended earlier or was already absorbed. So sort, then one pass. O(n log n) for the sort.
Sort, then either extend the last merged booking or start a new one.
For 9 to 11, 1 to 4, 3 to 6, 11 to 12: sorted it’s 1-4, 3-6, 9-11, 11-12. 3-6 overlaps 1-4, so 1-6. 9-11 starts after 6, new booking. 11-12 touches 11, so 9-12. Result 1-6 and 9-12.
For 1-10 and 2-3: 2-3 overlaps, and the max keeps the end at 10. If I had just set the end to 3, that would be a bug.
O(n log n) time and O(n) for the output.
